answer.answer: Five incidents are open in three fields, costing about 31,800 barrels of oil, about $2.2 million in lost revenue at an assumed $70 a barrel. High severity: W-12 (Dune Field) is shut in with casing pressure that will not bleed off [1], W-36 (Salt Flat Field) is shut in after a flowline leak [2], and W-34 (Salt Flat Field) runs on a reduced choke after sand erosion [3]. Others: W-25 (Wadi Field) has pump vibration and runs slower [4], and W-05 (Dune Field) has wellhead pressure swings and is still producing [5].

answer.answer: W-17, a Wadi Field well, was shut in from 4 March 2026 until it restarted on 18 March 2026, after its electric pump (ESP) tripped on a motor overload with phase current imbalance [1]. The workover (a repair job with a rig) found motor winding insulation breakdown and light scale on the pump stages, and the crew replaced the pump and its cable with a new Varenta VL-538 pump [2]. The outage and repair together lost about 17,942 barrels of oil, about $1,256,000 in lost revenue at an assumed $70 a barrel [3][4].
